meta.title: Uncle Dan and the Golf Forecast

paragraphs: On Thursday evening, Uncle Dan came to visit the family. He is Dad's older brother. He loves golf. He brought two golf clubs and a small bag of balls. "I want to play golf with you this weekend," he said to Dad. "We can play almost anywhere, but we need good weather," said Dad. "Let's check the forecast," said Lily.

Lily and Tom sat at the table with Dad's phone. The forecast had three days. Each day had a small picture. "Friday: wet in the morning and cloudy in the afternoon, twenty-six degrees." The picture showed a gray cloud with three drops of rain. "Saturday: dry and sunny, with almost no wind, thirty degrees." The picture showed a big yellow sun. "Saturday is perfect for golf!" said Tom.

Lily read the last part of the forecast. "Sunday: warm, with a few clouds, and maybe a small shower in the evening, twenty-nine degrees." "Maybe means that it is not sure," said Tom. "So Saturday is the best day for golf." "I like the forecast," said Uncle Dan. "We will play on Saturday at seven o'clock, before the sun is too hot." "Can we come, too?" asked Lily.

Uncle Dan smiled and told them a fact. "A golf ball has many small holes on the outside," he said. "They help the ball fly far, and they help it fly straight." "That is a lovely fact," said Lily. "Do you want to know another fact?" asked Dad. "A golf game is long, so we will bring water and hats."

On Friday, it rained in the morning, as the forecast said. Lily put on one boot, and then she put on the other boot. She took Pip for a short walk. The boots kept her feet dry, but Pip's feet were wet. On Saturday, the sky was blue, and the wind was soft. Dad, Uncle Dan, Lily, and Tom walked to the golf course at seven o'clock. Dad carried the clubs, and Tom carried the bottles of water. Uncle Dan carried the small bag of balls. Pip stayed at home with Mom. He slept in the sun.
